guidance: A legal classification with consequences. Attribute it ("X described it as") rather than asserting it, unless a body with authority to make the determination has done so.
Contested between 'incursion', 'operation' and 'invasion' in most live conflicts. Attribute, and state who is using the word.
A determination made by courts and specific bodies under the Genocide Convention. Never assert; attribute to the body or party making the claim, with the date.
A designation, not a description. Name the designating government or body and the date of designation.
The choice between 'riot', 'protest', 'uprising' and 'insurrection' carries a judgement. Prefer the most specific factual description of what occurred, and attribute contested labels.
In the U.S. this is a determination made after the fact by the NBER business cycle dating committee. Do not assert it in advance of that determination.
No authoritative body makes this determination. Attribute it to whoever is using it, or describe the underlying dispute instead.
A legal conclusion. Unless a court has ruled, say what statute is alleged to be violated and who alleges it.
Meaningless without a baseline — the same figure is a cut against a request and an increase against the prior year. State the baseline every time.
Reserve for outlays. For earlier funding stages name the stage: requested, authorized, appropriated, obligated. This is the single most common conflation in budget coverage.
Loaded and rarely precise. Describe the instrument — loan, guarantee, equity purchase, grant — and its terms.
Implies a magnitude the number may not support. Give the figure and the comparison period instead.
